body:
Elliot Price: starting docs plan for Usage Insights (route+model breakdown + top drivers + export). want to get ahead of beta enablement so we’re not scrambling for screenshots. what’s the latest on UI being stable enough for capture?

Wei Chen: +1. also need clarity on terminology — are we calling it “route”, “endpoint”, or “API route”? DevEx feedback was that “route” is ambiguous.

Alex Martinez: yeah, community folks interpret “route” as “my app’s URL route” 😅. I’d vote “API endpoint” in headings, but keep “route (API path)” in tooltips. can we align w/ console labels?

Dylan Brooks: console currently says “Route” in filters/tables (matches backend dimension). we can add helper text in UI: “API route (e.g. /v1/chat/completions)”. I’m fine if docs use “API route” consistently.

Elliot Price: cool, I’ll use “API route” as primary term, and call out that we normalize/templatize dynamic segments.

Elliot Price: for screenshots, can someone share where staging is at? ideally need:
- main breakdown table (Route x Model)
- drilldown view (one route, model list + token/cost columns)
- top cost drivers card(s)
- export flow (modal + “export started” toast + download link)
- permission denied state (if cost hidden / no export permission)

Alicia Perez: design is final-ish, but a few polish items still open (empty states + banner styling). I can share Figma frames now as placeholders if that helps.

Wei Chen: Figma placeholders would be useful for drafting structure, but we’ll still need real console captures for launch/GA.

Chloe Martin: backend for export is still being wired. UI can show the export button behind the flag, but the async job status might change slightly. breakdown table + filters are stable.

Elliot Price: ok. can we do a 2-step approach:
1) draft article w/ Figma placeholders (labeled “beta UI subject to change”)
2) swap for real screenshots once flag is enabled in staging

Alex Martinez: works for me. for examples, let’s include:
- “why does my cost spike?” example: token_out up + cache hit down
- “why are totals not matching invoice?” troubleshooting bullets (time range, lag, rounding)
- export CSV example + how finance can pivot by route/model

Elliot Price: yup. I’ll add a troubleshooting section. also need the export CSV columns list (at least in docs as “what you’ll see”). who owns the latest spec?

Dylan Brooks: there’s a working CSV spec doc in Drive (I’ll DM link). columns roughly: time_bucket_start, workspace, project, deployment_mode, region, route, model_family, model_version, tokens_in, tokens_out, cache_hit_tokens, cache_miss_tokens, retries, fallbacks, cost_usd. rounding is still being debated.

Wei Chen: for docs we should avoid promising exact columns if still in flux. maybe describe as “columns may vary; see exported file headers” + list the key ones.

Elliot Price: agreed. but we should at least document definitions for tokens_in/out, cache hit rate, retries, fallbacks.

Chloe Martin: on definitions: retries = request attempts beyond the first within Redwood (client retries won’t be fully visible unless they hit us). fallbacks = model substitution due to policy/capacity. we’ll have a “fallback_model” dimension in drilldown but not sure if it lands in v1 export.

Alex Martinez: call that out explicitly. customers ask “is this my retry logic or yours?” all the time.

Elliot Price: noted.

Elliot Price: action items:
- Alicia: share Figma frames link in thread
- Dylan/Chloe: once staging has flag enabled, drop a couple screenshot candidates (or point me to a staging account I can access)
- Alex: send me 1–2 “recommended levers” links (batching/caching/routing) we want to point to from docs
- Wei: can you review terminology + troubleshooting draft once I paste it?

Alicia Perez: here’s Figma frames: https://figma.com/file/console-usage-insights (Usage Insights > Beta) — frames include breakdown table, top drivers, export modal, and “no permission” state.

Alex Martinez: links for levers:
- caching/prefix cache overview (internal doc for now): https://docs.redwoodinference.ai/optimize/caching
- batching guide: https://docs.redwoodinference.ai/optimize/batching
- routing/fallback policies: https://docs.redwoodinference.ai/console/routing

Wei Chen: happy to review. when you draft, include a short “Data freshness” note + what the banner means (customers will screenshot that and ask Support).

Dylan Brooks: re screenshots: I can probably get you real captures tomorrow from staging. need to confirm allowlist + a test workspace with data. will update.

Elliot Price: perfect. target is to have a doc draft ready by end of week so we can link it from beta release notes.
